note: Pre-registered parameters for the disclosed self-trading experiment. AMENDED TWICE on 19 Aug 2026 and a third time on 20 Aug. First, after five trades: a single pivot made every trade near it flip direction, so the wallet alternated buy/sell/buy/sell like a metronome. Replaced with a band — buy while the USDC balance falls, sell while it rises, reverse only at 10 and 20 — which produces runs of one to three trades in the same direction. seed_usdc was removed in the same amendment: it governed nothing in the worker and named a figure the wallets were never funded to. The band is self-funding — below the lower bound an arm sells tokens for USDC, above the upper it buys — so no arm ever needs topping up, and the only consumable is gas. Both changes are recorded as events in the log and the rules hash moved with them, which is what the hash is for. This file is committed BEFORE the first trade; its canonical hash is written into the market D1 rules row, and the worker refuses to trade unless its bundled copy hashes to the same value. Changing anything here is a visible commit that the running worker will reject until the row is updated on purpose. See docs/drafts/wash-worker-blueprint.md and the diary entry that names this what it is: wash trading, disclosed. THIRD AMENDMENT, 20 Aug 2026, after the BYKO arm halted on its own price-deviation guard at 64.1%: all eight of its trades had been buys and not one a sell. The wallet was funded to $34.32 while its band tops out at $20, and the rule 'buy while the balance is above the upper bound' then obliged it to spend $24 in one direction before it could ever reverse. Twenty-four dollars into a pool holding $123 is a 64% price move, so the guard was tripped by the strategy's own design rather than by anything going wrong. Two parameters are added and the guard itself is NOT touched: it fired correctly, and widening a limit because it caught something is the exact move this project exists to criticise. run_reverse_pct makes a run reverse once the pool price has moved that far from where the run began, so the excursion is bounded by price rather than by how much cash happens to sit in the wallet. max_trade_pct_pool clamps the drawn size to a share of the pool's USDC reserve: $9 was 6% of this pool and moved the price ~12% in a single trade, which would spend a whole run in one step, while the same $9 in a deep pool would be nothing. An instrument has to scale to what it measures.
